$comment: The form decision layer. selection-rules.json answers WHICH REPRESENTATION a collection gets and card-rules.json answers WHICH CARD once the answer is cards; this file answers the question that used to be taste on the other side of the screen: once a zone CAPTURES INPUT, which kind of form it is, what it is built from, and how it commits. A kind is chosen by four things and nothing else: how many fields, how familiar the task is, whether the surrounding context has to stay visible, and who commits the change. Consolidated 2026-08-23 from GOV.UK (question pages, one thing per page, error summary, conditional reveal, marking the minority), SAP Fiori (object page create/edit mode, footer bar, draft handling), Baymard (label placement, inline validation timing), NN/g and GitLab Pajamas (saving and feedback), Carbon and Polaris (form structure), and WCAG 2.2 (1.3.5, 3.3.1, 3.3.7, 3.3.8). The survey behind it is docs/RESEARCH-FORMS.md. check-screen-spec.mjs enforces it: a zone whose task is input must say which kind of form it is and how it commits, and may only use a kind some matching rule chooses.

explicit.means: The user presses a named button and the record changes then, not before.
explicit.use: Records: anything another person or another screen reads afterwards.

per-row.means: Each control applies on change, on its own, with its own feedback.
per-row.use: Settings: knobs read rarely and changed one at a time.

autosave.means: The form saves itself after a pause in typing and states when it last did.
autosave.use: Drafts: long, resumable work where 'continue later' is expected.

none.means: Nothing is committed at all: the input narrows or searches what is already there.
none.use: Filters and search. They own no Save, no dirty state and no error summary.

standalone.means: The form is the screen. Nothing behind it needs reading.

over-list.means: Opened from a collection the user was working in.

beside-context.means: The record, list or document behind it must stay readable while the fields are filled in.

in-place.means: The field is edited where it is read, inside other content.

dialog.means: A modal form over the screen that opened it.
dialog.useWhen: 1 to 6 fields, routine, reversible, and the list behind it is the context.
dialog.notWhen: The record has named sections, or the page behind it has to be read while typing.
owes: A primary that names the event, never 'Submit'.
Every field reachable without the dialog scrolling past its own actions.

panel.means: The same form in a side panel, with the context still on screen.
panel.useWhen: Editing while the record or the list behind it stays readable.
panel.notWhen: The form is longer than the panel scrolls comfortably, or nothing behind it matters.
owes: The panel keeps its own footer actions; the page's actions stay for the page.

page.means: A page-sized form: sections under a header, actions in a footer bar.
page.useWhen: 7 or more fields, or the form has named sections, or the form IS the screen's job.
page.notWhen: Three fields, which a dialog does without a route change; or an unfamiliar sequence, which is a wizard.
owes: Sections with real legends once there is more than one group.
An error summary above the first field on a failed submit.
Actions pinned in the footer bar, reachable without scrolling to the end.

wizard.means: One sequential task split into revealed steps, with a check-answers step at the end.
wizard.useWhen: Long AND unfamiliar, order matters, and a summary is owed before the commit.
wizard.notWhen: Two steps, or a routine the user repeats: a wizard there is a page form with extra clicks (Fiori).
owes: A review step that repeats every answer with a Change link (WCAG 3.3.7: never ask twice).
Steps addressable in the URL, so a reload does not restart the task.

question.means: One question per screen, Continue underneath.
question.useWhen: Public or infrequent users, branching questions, low confidence, or a flow that must survive being abandoned (GOV.UK one thing per page).
question.notWhen: Internal users who repeat the flow daily: they pay for it in clicks.
owes: Its own URL per question, so back and bookmark both work.
question.waitingFor: a public-facing flow in one of the products; internal screens have never needed it
question.note: Was `planned` with no `opensWhen` — a claim with no expiry, which is how a status outlives the thing it described. Marked built on 2026-08-26 when a specimen was written for it out of registry parts only. Composable today from a heading and two Buttons; the kind is a LAYOUT decision (one question per screen), not a part the system was missing.

review.means: Every answer restated before an irreversible commit, each with a link back to where it was given.
review.useWhen: The submit cannot be taken back, or the user has been away between steps.
review.notWhen: Nothing is irreversible and the whole form is on one screen anyway.
owes: Change links whose accessible name carries the field, not five bare 'Change' links.

settings.means: Grouped sections of explained knobs, each applied on its own.
settings.useWhen: Configuration read rarely and changed deliberately; every row says what it actually affects.
settings.notWhen: The rows are really records to manage, which is a list.
owes: No page-level Save: a page that applies some rows and asks for Save on others is a page nobody trusts.

auth.means: Sign in, sign up, reset, verify.
auth.useWhen: The screen's only job is identifying the user.
auth.notWhen: Anything with a second purpose on the same screen.
owes: Paste into the password field stays allowed and the browser may fill it (WCAG 3.3.8).
Error copy that does not say which half of the pair was wrong.

inline.means: One field edited where it is read.
inline.useWhen: A single value on a record the user is already looking at: a title, an owner, a status.
inline.notWhen: Several fields at once, which is a panel or a dialog.
owes: The read and edit states occupy the same space, so nothing below moves when editing starts.
inline.waitingFor: a second product asking for it; RenameDialog covers the one live case
inline.note: Was `planned` with no `opensWhen` — a claim with no expiry, which is how a status outlives the thing it described. Marked built on 2026-08-26 when a specimen was written for it out of registry parts only. <InlineText> is the part, and it has been in the registry since before this status was written.

bulk.means: One change applied to the records the user selected.
bulk.useWhen: The same edit across many rows, with the count stated in the copy.
bulk.notWhen: The change differs per record: that is editing each one.
owes: The number of records in the confirm copy, and what happens to the ones that fail.
bulk.waitingFor: a product with a selection model in a list
bulk.note: Was `planned` with no `opensWhen` — a claim with no expiry, which is how a status outlives the thing it described. Marked built on 2026-08-26 when a specimen was written for it out of registry parts only. <BatchActions> states the count and <Modal actions> asks the question; both exist.

grid.means: Editing across a collection, in the cells themselves.
grid.useWhen: Editing many records is the primary task.
owes: A row that fails says so in the row, not in a dialog about the whole grid.

confirm.means: Yes or no on a stated consequence.
confirm.useWhen: A destructive or irreversible action needs an explicit second press.
confirm.notWhen: The user has to type anything: that is a verified confirm.
owes: The consequence in the copy, and the real verb on the button.

verified-confirm.means: A destructive action gated behind typing the thing's own name.
verified-confirm.useWhen: Unrecoverable and wide: deleting a workspace, revoking everyone's access.
verified-confirm.notWhen: Recoverable actions, where typing is theatre and trains people to type through warnings.
owes: The exact string to type, quoted, and a primary that stays inert until it matches.
verified-confirm.waitingFor: a product with an unrecoverable, wide-blast-radius action
verified-confirm.note: Was `planned` with no `opensWhen` — a claim with no expiry, which is how a status outlives the thing it described. Marked built on 2026-08-26 when a specimen was written for it out of registry parts only. <Modal> takes children and `actions.confirmDisabled`, so the field and the armed button are one dialog. This is the same unblocking as lifecycle-rules' `confirm-typed` on the same day: the blocker was that no dialog both took input and coloured its commitment, and folding FormModal into Modal made one that does.

upload.means: Files plus the metadata that describes them.
upload.useWhen: What is being captured IS the file, and the fields explain it.
upload.notWhen: Files alone with nothing to say about them: that is the control, not a form.
owes: Progress per file, and a failure that names the file rather than the batch.

draft.means: A long form that saves itself and can be left.
draft.useWhen: Resumable work where 'continue later' is expected and losing it is the real risk.
draft.notWhen: Short forms: autosave there surprises more than it helps.
owes: A status line that says when it last saved, and what happens when a save fails.

composer.means: Free text plus attachments, sent rather than saved.
composer.useWhen: The result is a message in a thread.
composer.notWhen: The result is a record with fields.
owes: Enter sends or Enter breaks the line, decided once and stated.

filter.means: Input that narrows a collection already on screen.
filter.useWhen: Nothing is committed: the values change what is shown, and are gone next time unless the screen remembers them.
filter.notWhen: The values persist as a record: that is a real form.
owes: A way to clear everything, and the current narrowing visible without opening a menu.

search.means: One query field, submitted to find.
search.notWhen: More than one criterion, which is a filter.
owes: An empty result that says what was searched for.

rules.because: Up to eight routine fields opened from a list is a dialog: the list is the context, and a route change to a page loses it. Past that the dialog scrolls its own actions off screen (HF1).
When the thing behind the form has to stay readable, a modal is the wrong container: it covers exactly what the user is copying from.

Past six fields a dialog scrolls its own actions off screen and has nowhere to put sections (Fiori: create page, not create dialog). Steps are not automatic here: they are earned by unfamiliarity (F4), not by length.
Long AND unfamiliar is the one case steps earn their clicks: the user cannot judge the whole form at once, so it is revealed a step at a time.
Long but familiar is a page form. Forcing steps on a routine the user repeats weekly only adds clicks (Fiori).
Public users under load do better with one thing per page: it survives interruption, branches cleanly and handles errors one at a time (GOV.UK).
Applying each control on its own IS the settings model; anything else with a per-row commit is a settings screen that has not admitted it.
Autosave belongs to work that is long enough to lose. A short form that saves itself leaves the user unsure anything happened.
Input that commits nothing is a narrowing, not a form: no Save, no dirty state, no error summary.
One value on a record already on screen is edited where it is read; opening a dialog for it costs more than the edit.

A form with no fields of its own is a decision, not a capture: it asks yes or no, asks the user to type the name of what they are destroying, or restates the answers already given before an irreversible submit.
A short standalone capture is a page form or one of the specialised short screens; which one is decided by what it captures, not by its length.

hard.because: Nine or more fields in a dialog scroll the actions out of the viewport and leave sections nowhere to go (Fiori: create page).
A container with Cancel in its footer promises the change can be abandoned; autosave has already committed it.
A screen that commits nothing must not carry a Save: it teaches the user that Save sometimes means nothing.
Mixing per-row apply with a page-level Save on one screen is the save model nobody can predict (Pajamas: do not mix).

notes.say: four or more fields committed at once: a failed submit owes an <ErrorSummary> above the first field, focused, with a row per failure — marking fields in place only helps someone who can see the whole form at once (GOV.UK)
eight or more fields read as one undifferentiated column: group them into <FormSection>s whose legends say who or what each group is about, or split the form into steps
an autosaving form owes a <SaveStatus>: without it the user invents their own proof that the work is safe, usually by retyping it
a public audience on one long page is the case GOV.UK measured as failing: low-confidence users do better with one question per screen, and the flow survives being abandoned
a wizard's last step is a check-answers step (<WizardReview>): re-asking what was already answered is the WCAG 2.2 redundant-entry failure, and the summary is where it is usually broken
